page1.text: Using a thin connected circuit like a blood vessel, I see a memory I can't reach.

page2.text:
This was his memory.
At least, it isn't mine.
This is someone else's story.
It's so long ago that he doesn't think about it.
A memory so distant that he doesn't even try to recall it.
A memory so old that he can't even remember it.
They are...
The heavy shackles of a contract, set in stone, unable to be changed or retracted.

page3.text:
It's not like he wanted anything.
Rather, he was the type of person who could not stand many things.
He could not stand if there was someone crying near him.
He could not stand if there was someone hurt near him.
He could not stand if there was someone dying near him.
That was the only reason.
And for only that reason, he tried to save everyone within view.

page4.text:
He was so clumsy that it would make you nervous watching him.
But he would accomplish it in the end and change many a fate.
To that end, his life was full of blessedness.
The awkward, inelegant battles he fought had meaning.
For as much as he was hurt and stared down death, he was equally able to save people.

page5.text:
...But, there was one pitfall there.
Everyone within view.
Yet you cannot wholly look upon yourself.
So in the end...
He was not able to save the most important person of all, himself.

page6.text:
I don't know how it ended up like that.
No, it should be the other way around.
It was a wonder it didn't end up like that sooner.
And so, there was a terrible disaster.
Many people died, and many more faced death.
There was nothing he alone could do.
With so many deaths an inevitability before him...

page7.text: "Let me make a contract. I shall give you my life after death. I would take compensation now."

page8.text:
Yes, he made a contract with a mysterious thing known as the World.
Throwing away himself to save all those living here.
The birth of a hero.

page9.text:
That's it.
There's nothing after that.
Even if he is called a hero, it doesn't change what he does.
From the start, his objective wasn't to become a hero.
He merely needed a hero's power as part of the process.

page10.text:
Even then, his ending came quickly.
A savior is nothing but a nuisance to those who are not saved.

page11.text:
He understands his own powers and the extent of the world.
He accepts there are those that he can and cannot save.
And so he wanted those within sight to be happy, at least.
Others becried it as hypocrisy.
There were many who despised him for his narrow-mindedness.
Even then, the way that he silently pursued his ideals was something he should've been proud of.

page12.text:
But in the end...
He faced an uncompensated death, as per the contract.

page13.text: And in the end, he reached that place.

page14.text:
He had friends and a lover.
But cornered by his ideal, he lost it all.

page15.text:
With no place to go...
Carrying the voices of resentment with him, he continued to fight.
He knew of his fate heading towards death, but he used that to try to perform the miracles that were beyond his capacity.

page16.text:
...But, that comes to an end.
He arrives at the hill of swords.
The end of his battle came on a mound with rusted, ownerless blades.
